questions.title: Right-Aligned Star Triangle
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Use two inner loops per row: one for leading spaces and one for stars.
questions.problem_statement: Given N, print N rows. Row i contains i stars, preceded by N − i spaces. Do not print trailing spaces.
hints: The outer loop runs once per row, with i from 1 to N.
Inside it, one loop prints N − i spaces and a second loop prints i stars.
Use System.out.print inside the inner loops and System.out.println() at the end of each row.

questions.title: Hollow Square Frame
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Decide between a star and a space for each cell based on whether it lies on the border.
questions.problem_statement: Print an N × N square. Print * on the first and last rows and at the first and last positions of every other row. Print spaces inside the border. For N = 1, print one star.
questions.output_format: Print N rows of the hollow square.
hints: Use nested loops over rows i and columns j, both from 1 to N.
A cell is on the border when i == 1, i == N, j == 1, or j == N.
Print * for border cells and a space for all others.

extra_fields.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
extra_fields.output_format: Print N rows of the hollow square.

questions.title: Repeated Row Number Triangle
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Print the row number repeatedly, placing spaces only between values.
questions.problem_statement: Print N rows. Row i contains the number i repeated exactly i times, with one space between adjacent values.
hints: The inner loop runs i times on row i.
Print the row number i, not the column number.
Print a space before every value except the first one in the row.

questions.title: Alternating Binary Triangle
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Derive each value from its column position using the remainder operator.
questions.problem_statement: Print N rows. Every row starts with 1, and adjacent values alternate between 1 and 0. Separate values with one space.
hints: Row i contains i values.
The value at column j is 1 when j is odd and 0 when j is even.
j % 2 gives exactly that value.

extra_fields.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops

questions.title: Palindromic Number Pyramid
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Combine a leading-space loop with an ascending loop and a descending loop on each row.
questions.problem_statement: Print N rows. Row i contains the sequence 1, 2, …, i, followed by i − 1, i − 2, …, 1. Separate the digits with no spaces. Print N − i leading spaces before each row.
hints: Each row needs three inner loops: spaces, ascending digits, and descending digits.
The ascending loop goes from 1 to i.
The descending loop goes from i − 1 down to 1.

questions.title: Continuous Number Triangle
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Keep a counter outside the nested loops so numbering continues across rows.
questions.problem_statement: Print consecutive integers beginning at 1. Row i contains exactly i integers. Continue the sequence across row boundaries, with one space between adjacent integers.
hints: Declare int value = 1; before the outer loop.
Print value and then increase it inside the inner loop.
Because value is never reset, row i + 1 continues where row i ended.

questions.title: X-Shaped Star Pattern
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Place stars on both diagonals and stop each row after its last star.
questions.problem_statement: Print an N × N visual grid. A star appears wherever the row and column positions are equal or their sum is N + 1. All other positions are spaces. Do not print trailing spaces.
hints: Row i has stars at columns i and N + 1 − i.
Only loop up to the larger of those two columns, so no spaces follow the last star.
For even N, the diagonals never share a cell; for odd N, they meet in the middle row.

questions.title: Numbered Rectangle
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Print a rectangle where the value depends only on the column.
questions.problem_statement: Print R rows and C columns. Every row contains the integers from 1 through C in increasing order, separated by one space.
questions.input_format: R and C, each on a separate line.
questions.output_format: Print the R × C numbered rectangle.
hints: The outer loop runs R times and the inner loop C times.
Print the column number j in each cell.
Put a space before every value except the first in each row.

questions.title: Alternating Row Direction
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Compute each row's start value and loop forward or backward depending on the row.
questions.problem_statement: Print N rows containing consecutive integers from 1 through N². Odd-numbered rows are printed left to right, while even-numbered rows are printed right to left. Separate values with one space. Do not store the grid in an array.
hints: Row i covers the values (i − 1) × N + 1 through i × N.
For odd rows, loop upward through that range; for even rows, loop downward.
Keep the single-space separator rule the same in both directions.

questions.title: Pascal's Triangle
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Compute each Pascal value from the previous one in the same row, without storing rows.
questions.problem_statement:
Print the first N rows of Pascal's triangle. Each row begins and ends with 1. Every interior value equals the sum of the two values directly above it.

For row i, print exactly N − i leading spaces, followed by the row's values separated by single spaces. This spacing rule applies even when multi-digit values make the pattern look imperfectly centered. Do not print trailing spaces.
questions.output_format: Print N rows of Pascal's triangle.
questions.constraints:
1 ≤ N ≤ 15
All values fit in a Java long.
hints: Number the rows from 0; row r has r + 1 values, the first of which is 1.
Each next value in the same row is value * (r − k) / (k + 1), where k is the position of the current value.
Multiply before dividing so the division is always exact.

extra_fields.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
extra_fields.output_format: Print N rows of Pascal's triangle.

questions.title: Consecutive Prime Triangle
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Combine a prime-testing helper with a triangle layout and a running search position.
questions.problem_statement: Print N rows of consecutive prime numbers. Row i contains exactly i primes. Continue generating primes from where the previous row ended. Separate primes with one space.
hints: Write a static boolean isPrime(int n) helper.
Keep a candidate variable outside the loops and advance it until it is prime before printing.
After printing a prime, move the candidate forward by one so the next search starts after it.

questions.title: Multiplication Grid
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Compute each cell from both loop indices.
questions.problem_statement: Given N, print an N × N multiplication grid. The value at row i and column j is i × j, where both indices start at 1. Separate values with one space.
hints: Use nested loops with i for rows and j for columns.
Each cell is simply i * j.
Values are not padded, so columns do not need to line up.

questions.title: Mirrored Number Pyramid
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Print a descending run followed by an ascending run on each row.
questions.problem_statement: Print N rows. Row i contains the numbers i, i − 1, …, 1, 2, …, i. Separate values with no spaces between them. Print N − i leading spaces before each row, with no trailing spaces.
hints: After the leading spaces, loop from i down to 1.
Then loop from 2 up to i, so the 1 in the middle is printed only once.
Row 1 contains only the digit 1.

questions.title: Hollow Diamond
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Build each row from leading spaces, an outer star, inner spaces, and a second star.
questions.problem_statement: Given N, print a hollow diamond with 2N − 1 rows. In the upper half, row i (from 1 to N) has N − i leading spaces and then a star. For every row except the first, it also has 2i − 3 inner spaces followed by a second star. The lower half mirrors the upper half without repeating the middle row. Do not print trailing spaces.
hints: Handle the upper half with i from 1 to N, and the lower half with i from N − 1 down to 1.
Writing the row logic once in a helper method, such as static void printRow(int n, int i), avoids repeating it.
Row 1 has a single star; every other row has two stars with 2i − 3 spaces between them.

extra_fields.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops

questions.title: Butterfly Pattern
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Print two mirrored wings separated by a gap whose width depends on the row.
questions.problem_statement: Print 2N rows. In the upper half, row i (from 1 to N) contains i stars, then 2(N − i) + 1 spaces, then i more stars. The lower half repeats the upper-half rows in reverse order, so rows N and N + 1 are identical. Do not print trailing spaces.
hints: Write the row logic once, for example in a helper method that takes N and i.
Each row is i stars, 2(N − i) + 1 spaces, and i stars.
Print rows i = 1 to N, then rows i = N down to 1.

extra_fields.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops

questions.title: Concentric Number Square
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Compute each cell's layer from its distance to the nearest border.
questions.problem_statement:
Given N, print a square of size (2N − 1) × (2N − 1). The outer border contains N, the next layer contains N − 1, and values decrease toward the center until reaching 1. Calculate each cell's value from its row and column positions without using arrays.

Separate values with one space.
hints: Use 0-based indices i and j from 0 to 2N − 2.
The distance to the nearest border is the smallest of i, j, 2N − 2 − i, and 2N − 2 − j.
The cell's value is N minus that distance.

extra_fields.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops

questions.title: Symmetric Alphabet Diamond
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Use char arithmetic to print mirrored letter sequences in a diamond.
questions.problem_statement: Print an alphabet diamond with 2N − 1 rows. The upper half grows from A to the Nth letter, and each row mirrors its letters back toward A. Mirror the upper half to form the lower half. Use no spaces between letters and no trailing spaces.
hints: Row i (from 1 to N) has N − i leading spaces.
Print letters with (char) ('A' + k) for k from 0 to i − 1, then from i − 2 down to 0.
Print rows 1 to N, then rows N − 1 down to 1.

questions.title: Checkerboard Tiles
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Map each character position to its tile with integer division and alternate the tile symbol.
questions.problem_statement: A floor designer prints a square checkerboard made of N × N tiles. Each tile is K characters wide and K rows tall. Number tile rows and tile columns from 0. A tile is filled with # when its tile-row plus tile-column is even, and with . when it is odd, so the top-left tile is #. Print N × K rows of N × K characters with no spaces between them. Calculate each character from its row and column positions without using arrays.
questions.input_format: N and K on separate lines.
hints: Loop over character rows i and character columns j, both from 0 to N × K − 1.
The tile containing a character is at tile-row i / K and tile-column j / K.
Print # when (i / K + j / K) % 2 == 0, otherwise print .

extra_fields.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
extra_fields.input_format: N and K on separate lines.

questions.title: Prime Staircase With Alternating Direction
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Print a run of primes in reverse without storing them, by locating the run's end and stepping backward.
questions.problem_statement: Generate consecutive prime numbers and print them in N rows. Row i contains i primes. Print odd-numbered rows in increasing order and even-numbered rows in decreasing order. Continue generating primes across rows; do not use arrays or collections to store them.
questions.output_format: Print the prime staircase, separating values with one space.
hints: Write helpers isPrime, nextPrime (first prime above a value), and previousPrime (first prime below a value).
For each row, first find the row's last prime by calling nextPrime i times from where the previous row ended.
For an even row, print from that last prime downward using previousPrime; for an odd row, print upward from the first.

extra_fields.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
extra_fields.output_format: Print the prime staircase, separating values with one space.

questions.title: Alternating Concentric Layers
questions.module: Module 08: Pattern Printing with Nested Loops
questions.objective: Compute each cell's layer number and use its parity to choose a symbol.
questions.problem_statement: Print a square of size (2N − 1) × (2N − 1). The outermost layer contains 1, the next layer contains 2, and values increase toward the center. Print odd-numbered layers as * and even-numbered layers as #. The center belongs to layer N. Calculate each character from its row and column positions without using arrays. Separate characters with one space.
questions.output_format: Print the layered character pattern without trailing spaces.
hints: Use 0-based indices i and j from 0 to 2N − 2.
A cell's layer is 1 plus the smallest of i, j, 2N − 2 − i, and 2N − 2 − j.
Print * when the layer is odd and # when it is even.
